ca.title: FM reviews progress of Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway work
ca.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman inspected the ongoing construction of the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway at Devanahalli, Karnataka, as part of the Pragati Path Yatra Darshan programme. The project is a critical component of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor, aimed at enhancing high-speed connectivity and logistics efficiency across the southern region.
ca.keyPoints:
• Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman inspected the ongoing construction and development works of the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway at Devanahalli in Karnataka as part of the Pragati Path Yatra Darshan programme.
• The visit involved a review of the progress of road construction, traffic management measures, and infrastructure development associated with the Greenfield expressway project.
• The Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway is being developed under the Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I scheme to provide high-speed connectivity between Bengaluru and Chennai.
• The project is designed to strengthen connectivity to major industrial and logistics hubs, including Hoskote, Malur, Bangarpet, the Narasapura Industrial Area, and the Aerospace and Defence Parks.
• The expressway is expected to improve access to the proposed Multimodal Logistics Park at Dobbspet.
• The project originates at Hoskote near the junction of NH-4 and NH-207 in Karnataka.
• The Karnataka portion of the expressway was completed and became informally accessible to motorists in December 2024, while sections in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu remain under construction.
• The Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway has been identified as a priority corridor under the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.
• Bharatmala Pariyojana is a centrally-sponsored and funded road and highways project of the Government of India, managed by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, aimed at optimizing the efficiency of freight and passenger movement.
• The Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor is a flagship infrastructure project under the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, designed to stimulate manufacturing and economic growth in the southern states.
ca.whyInNews: The Union Finance Minister conducted an on-site review of the progress of the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway, a major infrastructure project under the Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS1 - Infrastructure and Connectivity | Mains: GS3 - Infrastructure: Energy, Ports, Roads, Airports, Railways etc.

ca.title: Kolkata’s damnatio memoriae moment
ca.summary: Damnatio memoriae was a formal Roman practice of condemning a person's memory by erasing their name, images, and inscriptions from public records and monuments. It served as a political tool to delegitimize disgraced emperors or elites, effectively sentencing them to historical oblivion.
ca.keyPoints:
• Damnatio memoriae involved the systematic destruction of statues, the recarving of inscriptions, and the prohibition of the deceased individual's name in public discourse.
• The Roman Senate, the supreme legislative body of the Roman Republic and Empire, held the authority to issue these decrees following the death of an unpopular ruler.
• Emperor Geta, who was murdered by his brother Caracalla in 212 CE, remains the most prominent example of this practice, as his image was scrubbed from the Arch of Septimius Severus.
• The practice functioned as a form of posthumous capital punishment, aiming to strip the individual of their legacy and social standing within the Roman state.
• Roman law, specifically the Twelve Tables and subsequent imperial edicts, provided the framework for controlling public memory and state-sanctioned propaganda.
• Similar practices have occurred globally, such as the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten being erased from king lists by his successors to restore traditional religious order.
• The structural challenge lies in the tension between historical preservation and the contemporary desire to sanitize public spaces of figures associated with systemic oppression.
• Modern digital equivalents include the right to be forgotten, where individuals seek to remove personal information from search engines to reshape their public identity.
ca.whyInNews: The concept has gained renewed academic attention due to modern debates regarding the removal of controversial historical statues and the digital erasure of public figures.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS1 - History of Ancient World | Mains: GS1 - Impact of historical narratives on contemporary social and political discourse.

ca.title: PM, Macron talk stresses economic security
ca.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron held bilateral talks in Nice, France, focusing on deepening economic security and technological cooperation. The leaders adopted an Innovation Roadmap 2030 and established a formal Dialogue on Economic Security to bolster supply chain resilience and strategic trade partnerships.
ca.keyPoints:
• India and France have adopted an Innovation Roadmap 2030 to provide a long-term direction to their bilateral partnership.
• The two nations established a new Dialogue on Economic Security to address critical supply chain vulnerabilities, particularly regarding critical minerals.
• Both sides called for the early implementation of the India-EU Free Trade Agreement, which was initially signed in February of this year.
• A High-Level Mechanism has been established with the objective of doubling bilateral trade within the next five years.
• The leaders agreed to create a Joint India-France AI Working Group to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence and related technologies.
• The discussions included specific focus areas for cooperation, including the SME, rail, and aviation sectors.
• Prime Minister Modi and President Macron co-inaugurated the Bharat Innovates 2026 event in Nice, emphasizing trust and technological collaboration.
• Nineteen agreements were signed between various entities to foster integration between the innovation ecosystems of India and France.
• The bilateral relationship has been formally elevated to a Special Strategic Partnership to reflect an enhanced level of cooperation.
• President Macron highlighted India's role as a reliable partner in the global geopolitical landscape during times of upheaval.
ca.whyInNews: The meeting between the two leaders in Nice, France, served as a platform to advance the India-France Special Strategic Partnership through new institutional frameworks and technology-focused agreements.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - International Relations | Mains: GS2 - Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India and/or affecting India's interests.

ca.title: The implementation of the four labour codes
ca.summary: The implementation of the four labour codes, enacted in 2019-20, has been completed with the notification of the rules in May. Despite this, the new framework faces significant criticism for failing to address structural vulnerabilities, leaving workers exposed to ambiguity in wage definitions, gig economy exclusions, and weak trade union recognition mechanisms.
ca.keyPoints:
• The four labour codes are The Code on Wages 2019, The Industrial Relations Code 2020, The Code on Social Security 2020, and The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020.
• The Code on Wages (Central) Rules provide only a vague definition of the floor wage and fail to clearly distinguish it from the minimum wage or provide a detailed framework for state consultations.
• The calculation of hourly wages by dividing the daily wage by eight is conceptually flawed as it ignores that workers may not find work for the remaining hours of the day.
• The Industrial Relations Code 2020 introduced Fixed-Term Employment (FTE), but the rules fail to specify a minimum tenure or limit the number of contract renewals, allowing for potential misuse.
• Registration of a trade union does not guarantee recognition, as the Industrial Relations Code (Central) Rules require a 30 percent membership threshold that is not present in the parent Act.
• The Social Security Code (Central) Rules fail to clarify the employment relationship for gig and platform workers, leaving them as part of the unorganised workforce without mandatory gratuity insurance.
• The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code (Central) Rules lack clarity on what constitutes core activity, creating ambiguity regarding the engagement of contract labour in core operations.
• The rules perpetuate gender bias by assigning a weight of 0.8 to an adult female compared to 1.0 for an adult male when calculating the consumption units of a four-member family.
• The Industrial Relations Code 2020 is a central legislation aimed at consolidating laws relating to trade unions, industrial disputes, and industrial employment.
• The Code on Social Security 2020 seeks to amend and consolidate laws relating to social security with the goal of extending coverage to all employees and workers in the organised and unorganised sectors.
ca.whyInNews: The Ministry of Labour and Employment has notified the rules for the four labour codes, marking the operationalization of the legislative framework after a six-year delay.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - Statutory Bodies and Labour Laws | Mains: GS3 - Issues relating to development and management of social sector/services relating to Labour.

ca.title: Lows of the land
ca.summary: The rejection of a Rajya Sabha nomination in Madhya Pradesh has sparked a controversy over the arbitrary application of disclosure norms for election candidates. The Returning Officer's decision to disqualify a candidate based on a private complaint—rather than a formal criminal charge—raises significant concerns regarding the integrity of the electoral process and the neutral functioning of the Election Commission of India.
ca.keyPoints:
• The Returning Officer's decision to reject the nomination based on a private complaint reeking of extreme arbitrariness and potential conspiracy undermines the fairness of the electoral process.
• Section 33A of the Representation of the People Act mandates the disclosure of only those criminal cases where a punishment of two years or more is prescribed and where charges have been formally framed by a court.
• Framing of charges is a specific judicial step that occurs only after the police have filed a formal charge sheet in a criminal matter.
• The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body established under Article 324, tasked with the superintendence, direction, and control of elections to ensure they are free and fair.
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the conduct of elections, including the qualification and disqualification of candidates and the disclosure of criminal antecedents.
• The Supreme Court has consistently held that the right to contest elections is a statutory right, and the rejection of a nomination must be based on clear, non-arbitrary legal grounds.
• The incident highlights a structural inconsistency where one candidate is permitted to amend affidavits while another is disqualified for similar or lesser grounds, suggesting a lack of uniform application of election rules.
• The core argument is that the Returning Officer's interpretation of disclosure requirements is legally flawed and effectively disenfranchises candidates based on non-material or non-criminal information.
ca.whyInNews: The nomination of Congress leader Meenakshi Natarajan for the Rajya Sabha election was rejected by the Returning Officer, prompting a Supreme Court intervention and allegations of procedural bias.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - Indian Polity and Governance | Mains: GS2 - Salient features of the Representation of People Act and the role of the Election Commission.

ca.title: FCRA Bill — expanding state control over civil society
ca.summary: The proposed Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks to significantly expand state control over civil society organizations by introducing stringent asset-management provisions and administrative procedures. The legislation risks undermining the operational autonomy of NGOs and charitable institutions by enabling the government to seize assets and funds under broadly defined public interest criteria.
ca.keyPoints:
• The 2026 Bill introduces a new Chapter IIIA that mandates the automatic cessation of FCRA registration if renewal is denied or delayed, effectively paralyzing organizations through procedural hurdles.
• Section 16A stipulates that upon cancellation or surrender of FCRA registration, all foreign contributions and assets derived from them automatically provisionally vest in a government-designated authority without prior judicial review.
• The designated authority is empowered to manage, transfer, or dispose of seized assets, with sale proceeds credited to the Consolidated Fund of India, effectively enabling executive confiscation.
• The 2020 amendments to the FCRA regime already imposed strict restrictions, including routing all foreign contributions through a single bank branch at the State Bank of India in New Delhi and reducing administrative expenditure limits from 50 percent to 20 percent.
• Between 2014 and 2026, approximately 22,000 FCRA licenses were cancelled, raising concerns about the systematic targeting of organizations, particularly those serving minority communities.
• Civil society organizations contribute significantly to the economy, accounting for approximately 2 percent of GDP and providing employment for 27 lakh jobs and 34 lakh full-time volunteers.
• The proposed Section 14B introduces automatic cessation of FCRA registration, while the abolition of Section 22 removes existing mechanisms for the disposal of assets of defunct organizations, creating legal uncertainty.
• The Bill faces constitutional challenges regarding Articles 14, 19(1)(c), 25, 26, 29, 30, and 300A, as it threatens the freedom of association and the autonomy of religious and educational institutions.
• The core argument is that the vague public interest standard and centralized enforcement under the amended Section 43 create a climate of fear that discourages civil society participation and threatens essential services like healthcare and education.
• The recommendation is that any regulation of foreign contributions must be accompanied by due process, independent oversight, and safeguards against arbitrary state action to prevent the erosion of civil society.
ca.whyInNews: The introduction of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on March 25, 2026, has sparked concerns regarding the potential for executive overreach and the systematic marginalization of non-governmental organizations.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - Indian Polity and Governance | Mains: GS2 - Role of NGOs and civil society in development and democracy.

ca.title: The release of the film Governor, which depicts the 1990s Indian financial crisis
ca.summary: The Indian film industry faces a structural tension between the pursuit of commercial box office success and the preservation of artistic craft. There is a growing call to decouple financial performance from critical evaluation, particularly for independent cinema, to foster a more sustainable creative ecosystem.
ca.keyPoints:
• The film Governor is a theatrical production centered on the financial crisis that occurred in India during the early 1990s.
• The narrative of Governor follows S. Venkitaramanan, the former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, who navigated the country through a period of national bankruptcy to stabilize the economy.
• The film Governor is directed by Chinmay D. Mandlekar and marks a significant entry in the landscape of independent Indian cinema.
• There is an urgent need to shift the discourse in Bollywood away from an obsession with box office returns, as financial management is the sole responsibility of the producer.
• Film critics and audiences should prioritize the evaluation of artistic craft and quality over commercial performance metrics.
• Independent filmmakers in India currently lack institutional mentorship and face significant systemic challenges in securing exhibition platforms for their work.
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central banking institution of India, established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, responsible for monetary policy and financial stability.
• S. Venkitaramanan served as the 18th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India from 1990 to 1992, a tenure defined by the balance of payments crisis and the initiation of structural economic reforms.
• The 1991 Indian economic crisis was a watershed moment that forced the transition from a closed, state-controlled economy to a liberalized market-oriented system under the New Economic Policy.
ca.whyInNews: The release of the film Governor, which depicts the 1990s Indian financial crisis, has prompted a public discourse on the commercial pressures facing independent filmmakers.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - Indian Economy | Mains: GS1 - Indian Society and the impact of globalization on cultural industries.

ca.title: Bacillary dysentery cases rise in Kerala
ca.summary: An outbreak of shigellosis, a highly contagious bacterial disease, has been reported across various districts in Kerala, with 34 cases confirmed in June alone. The infection, which causes severe gastrointestinal distress, is primarily spreading through contaminated water sources, including wells and borewells.
ca.keyPoints:
• Shigellosis, also known as bacillary dysentery, is a highly contagious bacterial diarrhoeal disease caused by the Shigella bacteria.
• The disease manifests as a severe form of diarrhoeal outbreak involving intestinal tissue invasion by the bacteria, causing highly infectious, bloody, and mucoid stools accompanied by high fever and severe abdominal cramps.
• The infection spreads through contaminated water, food, and contact from infected surfaces and is extremely infectious, with ingestion of as few as 10 to 100 bacteria capable of causing an infection.
• Transmission occurs rapidly via the fecal-oral route.
• In June alone, 34 cases have been reported across Kerala, with 47 people currently undergoing treatment in public and private hospitals.
• Wayanad district reported eight cases, including an outbreak at Mar Baselios Higher Secondary School where 514 children showed symptoms and water samples from the school's well were found to be highly contaminated.
• Other affected districts include Kozhikode (11 cases), Thiruvananthapuram (six cases), Alapuzha (three cases), Malappuram and Kannur (two cases each), and Kollam and Idukki (one case each).
• Shigellosis is a sporadic, recurring public health challenge in Kerala, with 133 cases reported in the previous year with zero deaths.
• The Kerala Department of Health and Family Welfare, led by the Health Minister, is responsible for monitoring, testing, and managing the outbreak through district-level medical surveillance.
• The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) under the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) monitors such outbreaks in India to ensure timely containment and public health response.
ca.whyInNews: The Kerala Health Ministry has reported a surge in shigellosis cases, with significant clusters identified in schools and multiple districts, prompting urgent public health surveillance.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS2 - Health and Sanitation | Mains: GS2 - Issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services relating to Health.

ca.title: From June 15, free bus ride for Kerala women, trans people
ca.summary: The Kerala Cabinet has approved the 'Priyadarshini' scheme, which provides free bus travel for women and transgender individuals on ordinary services of the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC). The initiative is universal, covering all women regardless of age or financial background, and is set to commence on June 15.
ca.keyPoints:
• Scheme Name: Priyadarshini.
• Beneficiaries: Women of all ages and transgender individuals.
• Applicability: Limited to ordinary services of the Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) in the first phase.
• Eligibility: Universal access, irrespective of financial background.
• Implementation Date: Effective from June 15.
• Policy Objective: Promoting gender equality and reducing the cost of public transit for marginalized and vulnerable groups.
ca.whyInNews: The state government is implementing this welfare measure to enhance the mobility and socio-economic inclusion of women and transgender persons in public transport.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS-2 - Governance and Social Justice | Mains: GS-2 - Government policies and interventions for development in various sectors and issues arising out of their design and implementation.

ca.title: Experts raise concerns over spike in C-section deliveries in Delhi
ca.summary: The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) data reveals a concerning rise in caesarean section (C-section) deliveries in Delhi, increasing from 23.6% in 2019-21 to 27.4% in 2023-24. Experts attribute this trend to a combination of medical factors, patient preferences for painless delivery, and potential profit-driven practices in the private healthcare sector.
ca.keyPoints:
• WHO recommendation: Ideal C-section rates should hover around 10% to mitigate risks to both mother and infant.
• Sectoral disparity: Private facilities report a significantly higher C-section rate (50.9%) compared to public facilities (19.6%).
• Medical drivers: Rising maternal age (conception in 30s), obesity, gestational diabetes, and hypertension are increasing the medical necessity for surgical intervention.
• Social and systemic factors: Patient preference for 'painless' delivery and defensive medical practices by doctors to avoid potential liability are contributing to the surge.
• Environmental concerns: Emerging research suggests a correlation between poor air quality and adverse pregnancy outcomes, potentially necessitating more surgical interventions.
• Proposed interventions: Experts advocate for better documentation of medical indications, improved labour support, mandatory second opinions for non-emergency cases, and increased transparency in private hospitals.
ca.whyInNews: The recent NFHS data highlights a significant deviation from the World Health Organization's (WHO) recommended C-section rate of approximately 10%, sparking a debate on medical ethics and healthcare infrastructure.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS Paper 2 - Social Justice (Health/Demographic Data) | Mains: GS Paper 2 - Issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services relating to Health.

ca.title: Will continue ‘very hard attacks’, says Trump as U.S., Iran trade fire
ca.summary: The geopolitical situation in the Middle East has escalated following a tit-for-tat military exchange between the U.S. and Iran, triggered by the downing of a U.S. military helicopter over the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict involves U.S. air strikes on Iranian defense infrastructure and retaliatory Iranian missile and drone attacks on U.S. bases across Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan.
ca.keyPoints:
• Military escalation: U.S. air strikes targeted Iranian air defense, ground control stations, and radar sites near the Strait of Hormuz.
• Retaliatory strikes: Iran targeted U.S. assets, including the Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, Al-Azraq base in Jordan, and Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait.
• Strategic geography: The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical global maritime chokepoint currently under Iranian control.
• Economic warfare: The U.S. has maintained a naval blockade on Iranian ports since April 13, described as a 'steel wall' to pressure Tehran.
• Diplomatic failure: Direct negotiations in Islamabad failed to produce a breakthrough, leading to the collapse of previous ceasefire efforts.
• Humanitarian impact: Reports indicate U.S. strikes on infrastructure, such as water reservoirs in Bamani Sirik, have disrupted essential services for the local population.
ca.whyInNews: The report highlights a significant breakdown in diplomatic efforts and a fragile ceasefire, marking a period of heightened military confrontation between the U.S. and Iran in the Persian Gulf region.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS1 - International Relations | Mains: GS2 - Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India's interests, Important International institutions, agencies and fora - their structure, mandate.

ca.title: Inclusion without abolition in China’s hukousystem
ca.summary: China's recent policy guidelines aim to extend basic public services to migrant workers at their place of actual residence, bypassing the traditional restrictions of the rigid hukou (household registration) system. While these reforms seek to integrate the massive floating population into urban welfare systems to boost domestic consumption and urbanization, deep-seated structural issues like local government fiscal constraints and regional welfare disparities continue to limit full integration. The strategy represents a shift toward inclusion and labor mobility without dismantling the state's foundational mechanism of social and demographic control.
ca.keyPoints:
• The hukou system, established in the 1950s as a mechanism of social control, classifies Chinese citizens into rural or urban categories based on their official place of registration, effectively acting as an internal passport that ties access to social services and welfare to one's registered hometown.
• According to China's National Bureau of Statistics, the country's floating population of rural migrants reached approximately 358 million at the end of 2023, representing roughly 25 percent of the total national population.
• The State Council's five-year people-centered urbanization action plan, instituted in July 2024, targets an increase in the permanent urban resident ratio from 66.16 percent (932.67 million) in 2023 to nearly 70 percent (approximately 987 million) by 2029.
• Recent reform guidelines deliberately de-emphasize the term hukou, mentioning it only once, and instead promote inclusive concepts such as 'permanent resident population' (changzhu renkou) and 'place of actual residence' (changzhu di) to decouple public service delivery from birth-registration status.
• Despite these policy shifts, structural barriers persist as local governments bear the primary financial burden of welfare delivery but remain heavily dependent on central fiscal transfers, a vulnerability exacerbated by the ongoing instability in the real estate sector which traditionally funded local budgets.
• Significant regional disparities complicate the reform, as wealthier coastal provinces maintain higher social insurance standards and contributions compared to poorer inland migrant-sending provinces, leading to unequal benefit payouts and lower reimbursement rates for migrant workers.
• The guidelines lack binding mandates for employers in the rapidly growing gig economy—which comprises over 200 million flexible and platform workers out of a 740 million workforce—leaving their social security enrollment largely to the discretion of local administrations.
ca.whyInNews: The State Council of China issued new guidelines directing local governments and megacity administrations to provide basic public services—including education, housing, and medical insurance—to all residents based on their place of actual residence rather than their official hukou status.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS II - International Relations (Policies of countries affecting India's interests and global demographic trends) | Mains: GS II - Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections, issues relating to development and management of Social Sector/Services relating to Health, Education, Human Resources.

ca.title: China’s role in the international order
ca.summary: The article outlines China's positioning as a central hub of global diplomacy through high-level engagements with the other four permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. It highlights Beijing's advocacy for a UN-centered international system, strategic stability with the United States, and deepened coordination with Russia, while addressing the economic implications of its upcoming 15th Five-Year Plan.
ca.keyPoints:
• China advocates for a UN-centered international system, emphasizing multilateralism, non-aggression, and the resolution of global disputes through diplomatic dialogue rather than military intervention.
• The year 2026 marks the 30th anniversary of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation.
• With the initiation of its 15th Five-Year Plan spanning 2026 to 2030, China aims to position itself as a key contributor to global economic growth by opening its domestic markets and sharing development opportunities.
• The bilateral framework between the United States and China focuses on building constructive strategic stability, which seeks to balance cooperation, manage competition within defined limits, and navigate the critical issue of the Taiwan Strait under the One China principle.
• The United Nations Security Council, established in 1945 under the UN Charter, charges its five permanent members with the primary responsibility of maintaining international peace and upholding the post-WWII global order.
• In the context of India-China relations, both nations operate as large, strategically autonomous economies that must prioritize national development, seek common ground, and manage bilateral differences through mutual understanding.
• Global economic stability relies on deeply interconnected industrial and supply chains, requiring coordinated international efforts to address structural economic shifts and foster equitable global governance.
ca.whyInNews: A series of high-profile diplomatic visits to China by the leaders of France, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Russia between late 2025 and mid-2026 signals a period of intense bilateral engagement among the permanent members of the UN Security Council.
ca.upscAngle:
Prelims: GS II - Bilateral, regional and global groupings and agreements involving India
Mains: GS II - Effect of policies and politics of developed and developing countries on India's interests
MCQ watch: Distinguish between the One China Policy adopted by India and Western nations versus the One China Principle asserted by Beijing.
Must revise: UN Security Council veto power, China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness, India-China border peace agreements, Panchsheel Principles.
Likely Q: Analyze how the deepening strategic alignment between China and other permanent members of the UNSC impacts India's strategic autonomy and its geopolitical interests in the Indo-Pacific.

ca.title: cormorants
ca.summary: The highlighted clipping depicts a flock of Indian cormorants engaging in coordinated group hunting at Kandakadavu in Kochi, Kerala. This cooperative foraging behavior involves diving and herding fish collectively. For UPSC, this highlights avian behavioral ecology, wetland ecosystems of Kerala, and species-specific conservation profiles.
ca.keyPoints:
• HIGHLIGHTED CORE: A flock of Indian cormorants (Phalacrocorax fuscicollis) was observed exhibiting remarkable coordinated group hunting, diving beneath the water surface to herd and capture fish at Kandakadavu in Kochi, Kerala.
• SPECIES PROFILE: The Indian cormorant is a member of the cormorant family of waterbirds, distinguished by its bronze-brown plumage, slender bill, and blue-ringed eyes during the breeding season.
• CONSERVATION STATUS: The Indian cormorant is categorized as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species and is protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 of India.
• GEOGRAPHICAL DISTRIBUTION: It is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, inhabiting freshwater wetlands, large rivers, estuaries, reservoirs, and coastal tidal creeks.
• BEHAVIORAL ECOLOGY: Unlike solitary foragers, Indian cormorants frequently engage in social fishing, where a flock forms a semi-circle or line to drive fish schools into shallow waters for easier capture.
• WETLAND ECOSYSTEM CONNECT: The sighting location, Kochi, is adjacent to the Vembanad-Kole Wetland system, a designated Ramsar Site facing ecological pressures like pollution, land reclamation, and invasive species.
• EXAMINERS EYE: UPSC often tests unique behavioral traits of fauna (such as cooperative hunting or tool use) and may frame a question comparing cormorants with other wetland birds or asking about the ecological health of Kerala's backwaters.
• STATIC CONNECT: Key concepts to revise include the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands, the biogeography of Western Ghats estuaries, and the classification of aquatic avian species under India's National Action Plan for Conservation of Migratory Birds.
ca.whyInNews: A photographic feature captured Indian cormorants exhibiting highly synchronized cooperative hunting behavior amidst monsoon showers in Kochi, Kerala.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS3 - Species in News | Mains: GS3 - Biodiversity | Terms: Cormorant, Ramsar

ca.title: India’s road through Myanmar is one of engagement
ca.summary: The recent visit of Myanmar's President to India highlights a shift toward pragmatic engagement, prioritizing strategic connectivity and security over ideological isolation. India aims to balance its regional interests by maintaining infrastructure projects and security cooperation despite the ongoing political instability in Myanmar.
ca.keyPoints:
• India is pursuing a policy of pragmatic engagement with Myanmar, viewing it as a critical gateway for its Act East and Neighbourhood First policies.
• The Mahabodhi Temple in Bodh Gaya, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, serves as a symbol of shared civilisational ties between the two nations.
• The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects Kolkata to Sittwe by sea, then via the Kaladan River to Paletwa, and finally by road to Zorinpui in Mizoram.
• The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway aims to link Moreh in Manipur to Mae Sot in Thailand, with potential extensions to Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam.
• Bilateral trade stands at $1.95 billion for 2025-26, with plans to increase this through a rupee-kyat settlement mechanism and cooperation on critical minerals.
• Myanmar has pledged that its territory will not be used against India's interests, particularly regarding Indian insurgent groups and cybercrime networks.
• India has increased Mekong-Ganga ICCR scholarships for Myanmar students from 36 to 100 annually starting in 2026.
• The 109-km Paletwa-Zorinpui road remains incomplete due to mountainous terrain and internal conflict, with operationalization targeted for 2027.
• The Trilateral Highway, originally intended for completion by 2019, remains delayed due to security challenges and control of territory by armed groups.
• India's engagement is a strategic counterweight to China's growing influence in Myanmar, which has expanded through infrastructure financing and arms supplies since the 2021 coup.
• The Ministry of External Affairs manages these bilateral relations, while the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways oversees the execution of cross-border connectivity projects.
ca.whyInNews: Myanmar's President U Min Aung Hlaing visited India in mid-2026 for high-level talks, marking a significant diplomatic outreach amidst the country's internal political crisis.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS-1 (Art & Culture - UNESCO sites) | GS-2 (International Relations - India-Myanmar relations) | Mains: GS-2 (India and its neighbourhood-relations) | Key terms: Act East Policy, Neighbourhood First, Kaladan Multi-Modal Project, Trilateral Highway, Rupee-Kyat Settlement, Mekong-Ganga Cooperation

ca.title: Securing India against the threat of a ‘Mythocalypse’
ca.summary: The emergence of 'Mythos-class' AI models, capable of autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploitation, poses a significant threat to India's critical digital infrastructure. The article argues for a robust regulatory framework, including an AI accountability model and enhanced cybersecurity infrastructure, to mitigate risks from advanced, non-human-understandable AI systems.
ca.keyPoints:
• Anthropic has stated that its Claude Mythos model can outperform human experts at certain cybersecurity tasks.
• Mythos is fundamentally different from a standard Large Language Model because it acts as a zero-day at scale, discovering and exploiting flaws in code that are unknown to human operators.
• Mythos discovered long-standing bugs that had eluded human experts and automated fuzzing tools for decades, including a 16-year-old flaw in the Linux kernel.
• India needs a frontier AI accountability framework, modelled on California's SB 53 and the EU AI Act, tailored to Indian conditions.
• Any AI company operating in India whose model exceeds defined thresholds for compute, autonomy, or cyber capability should disclose capability evaluations and known harms to the proposed India AI Safety Institute (IAISI).
• India has built a distinctive world-class digital front end through the India Stack, including UPI, Aadhaar, and the Account Aggregator framework.
• India currently lacks a dedicated body to test AI models against Indian threat scenarios, as the IndiaAI Mission is primarily focused on development rather than safety evaluation.
• The cybersecurity workforce gap in India is estimated at more than 6,00,000 professionals, and patch cycles for public sector banks are measured in months rather than hours.
• A defensive AI partnership, potentially a 'Defensive AI Quad' with the U.S., U.K., and Japan, is recommended to secure access to Mythos-class capabilities for testing critical infrastructure.
• The government should establish a ₹15,000-20,000 crore critical sector cybersecurity upgradation fund to support legacy modernisation in public sector banks and develop sovereign defensive AI models.
• The Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) 2023 should be leveraged to ensure meaningful disclosure of AI risks and capabilities.
ca.whyInNews: The rapid advancement of autonomous AI models capable of identifying and exploiting system vulnerabilities has necessitated a shift in India's cybersecurity policy from reactive patching to proactive, AI-driven defense.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: GS 3 — Science and Technology (AI, Cybersecurity) | Mains: GS 3 — Challenges to internal security through communication networks, role of media and social networking sites in internal security challenges, basics of cyber security | Key terms: Mythos-class AI, IndiaAI Mission, India Stack, DPDPA 2023, Zero-day vulnerability, Defensive AI Quad, IAISI

ca.title: The Indian cormorant (Phalacrocorax fuscicollis)
ca.summary: The Indian cormorant (Phalacrocorax fuscicollis) exhibits sophisticated cooperative hunting behaviors, utilizing group coordination to herd and capture fish. This ecological phenomenon highlights the complex social structures and adaptive survival strategies prevalent among avian species in Indian wetlands.
ca.keyPoints:
• Indian cormorants are gregarious birds known for their highly synchronized group hunting tactics.
• They utilize collective movement to corral schools of fish, increasing the efficiency of their foraging efforts.
• These birds are primarily found in inland wetlands and coastal areas across the Indian subcontinent.
• The species serves as an important bio-indicator for the health of aquatic ecosystems and water quality.
• Their presence in urban or semi-urban water bodies like those in Kochi underscores the importance of preserving local biodiversity corridors.
ca.whyInNews: A flock of Indian cormorants was observed engaging in remarkable coordinated hunting behavior amidst monsoon showers at Kandakadavu in Kochi, drawing attention to their unique ecological habits.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper III (Environment & Ecology). Prelims focus: Species identification, wetland ecosystems, and animal behavior. Mains themes: Biodiversity conservation, impact of urbanization on avian habitats, and the role of indicator species in ecosystem monitoring.

ca.title: ‘Saheli’ cards for free bus travel prove elusive for trans persons in Delhi
ca.summary: The Delhi government's 'Saheli' scheme, intended to provide free bus travel for women and transgender persons, is facing significant implementation hurdles. Despite official policy, transgender applicants are frequently denied pink cards due to administrative confusion, lack of awareness among ground-level staff, and systemic technical limitations in card issuance systems.
ca.keyPoints:
• The 'Saheli' scheme was launched on March 2, 2025, to provide free travel benefits to women and transgender individuals on Delhi city buses.
• Transgender applicants report systemic denial of pink cards at distribution centres, with officials often incorrectly citing gender-based eligibility criteria.
• Administrative discrepancies persist as some officials claim the scheme is restricted to women, despite clear government mandates including transgender persons.
• Technical barriers exist in the backend systems, which often only recognize 'female' gender markers on Aadhaar cards, excluding those identifying as transgender.
• There is a significant gap between policy formulation and ground-level implementation, exacerbated by a lack of sensitization and training for frontline transport department staff.
ca.whyInNews: The issue gained prominence following reports from 'The Hindu' revealing that despite the official launch of the 'Saheli' scheme, transgender residents are being systematically denied access to free travel cards at various distribution centres in Delhi.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II (Social Justice/Governance): Issues relating to the development and management of social sector/services relating to Health, Education, Human Resources. Mains Themes: Inclusive governance, rights of transgender persons, implementation gaps in welfare schemes. Key terms: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019; Right to Equality (Article 14, 15); Administrative accountability; Inclusive public transport policy.

ca.title: Bengal govt. accepts Odisha CM’s request to drop ‘Dham’ from Digha temple name
ca.summary: The West Bengal government has decided to remove the term 'Dham' from the name of the Jagannath temple in Digha following concerns raised by the Odisha Chief Minister. The decision aims to respect religious sentiments regarding the sanctity of the 'Char Dham' in Hindu tradition and seeks to improve inter-state cultural harmony.
ca.keyPoints:
• The temple, originally inaugurated as 'Jagannath Dham' by the previous West Bengal government, will be renamed 'Sri Sri Jagannath Mandir Cultural Centre'.
• The decision follows a formal request from the Odisha Chief Minister, emphasizing that the term 'Dham' is traditionally reserved for the four sacred abodes in Sanatana Dharma.
• The move is framed as a corrective measure to address objections raised by religious authorities and political leaders regarding the nomenclature of the replica temple.
• The incident highlights the intersection of religious symbolism, state identity, and federal cooperation between neighboring Indian states.
• The West Bengal government stated that the facility will continue to function as a cultural and religious centre, ensuring that worship remains unaffected.
ca.whyInNews: The West Bengal government announced the renaming of the Digha Jagannath temple to remove the word 'Dham' after the Odisha Chief Minister expressed concerns over the misuse of the term.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II (Polity & Governance): Federalism, Inter-state relations, and the role of cultural/religious symbols in public policy. Prelims: Understanding the concept of 'Char Dham' in Hinduism.

ca.title: Maharashtra Cabinet nod to increase depts. from 33 to 45
ca.summary: The Maharashtra Cabinet has approved the restructuring of its administrative framework by increasing the number of administrative departments from 33 to 45. This policy shift aims to reduce the workload on departments managing multiple subjects, thereby enhancing governance efficiency and administrative coherence.
ca.keyPoints:
• The decision seeks to streamline the decision-making process by reducing the burden on departments currently handling diverse and multiple subjects.
• Restructuring is intended to facilitate more effective implementation of government schemes and improve coordination with field-level agencies.
• The current system of 33 departments often involves multiple sub-departments, which has historically led to inefficiencies in the distribution of manpower and work.
• The move is part of a broader administrative reform agenda to ensure better governance outcomes and improved service delivery at the state level.
ca.whyInNews: The Maharashtra Cabinet recently issued an official statement confirming the approval to expand the state's administrative departments from 33 to 45 to address operational bottlenecks.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II (Governance and Public Administration). Prelims: Focus on State Administration and Executive structure. Mains: Themes include Administrative Reforms, Decentralization, and Efficiency in Public Service Delivery. Key terms: Administrative restructuring, Governance, Public Policy Implementation, and State Executive.

ca.title: Shah calls for joint action by 3 States to rejuvenate Yamuna
ca.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah has mandated a coordinated, tri-state action plan between Delhi, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh to expedite the rejuvenation of the Yamuna river. The initiative focuses on integrated pollution management, infrastructure development, and continuous monitoring to address the river's critical ecological degradation.
ca.keyPoints:
• Shift from a fragmented approach to a unified, coordinated action plan involving Delhi, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh to ensure a standard ecological flow.
• Implementation of a memorandum of understanding between the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and the National Dairy Development Board to convert dairy waste into biogas and manure.
• Infrastructure targets include the completion of 129 existing sewage treatment plants (STPs) and the construction of 59 additional STPs by 2027.
• Aggressive desilting operations with 97% of the 28.57 lakh metric tons of silt already removed, with directives to repurpose extracted silt for construction to prevent re-entry into the river.
• Mandatory continuous monitoring of key water quality indicators, specifically Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), and Total Suspended Solids (TSS).
ca.whyInNews: The Union Home Minister chaired a high-level review meeting to address the persistent pollution crisis in the Yamuna river, emphasizing the need for inter-state cooperation.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper III (Environment & Ecology); Prelims focus: Water quality parameters (BOD, COD, TSS), river rejuvenation strategies, and urban waste management; Mains themes: Cooperative federalism in environmental governance, pollution abatement of trans-boundary rivers, and sustainable urban infrastructure.

ca.title: 24 Indians rescued from ship after  U.S. attack
ca.summary: Twenty-four Indian seafarers were rescued from the tanker Marivex following a U.S. missile strike off the coast of Oman. The vessel had been sanctioned by the United States due to its alleged links with Iran, highlighting the geopolitical tensions in the maritime trade routes of the Middle East.
ca.keyPoints:
• The incident involved the tanker Marivex, which was targeted by a U.S. missile strike in the waters off the southeastern coast of Oman.
• The U.S. had previously imposed sanctions on the vessel, citing its operational links to Iran.
• The rescued Indian crew members were safely relocated to Masirah Island, which is located off the coast of Oman in the Arabian Sea.
• The event underscores the risks to international shipping and seafarers in the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea region due to ongoing geopolitical conflicts.
• The rescue operation highlights the importance of international maritime safety protocols and the role of regional cooperation in crisis management.
ca.whyInNews: The rescue of 24 Indian nationals following a U.S. military strike on a sanctioned tanker near Oman has brought renewed attention to maritime security in the Indian Ocean Region.
ca.upscAngle: Prelims: Geography of the Arabian Sea, location of Masirah Island, strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman.

ca.title: NFHS Survey
ca.summary: The Union Health Ministry has clarified that the exclusion of certain indicators from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-6 preliminary factsheets is a strategic move to avoid data duplication. These indicators are being tracked through specialized national surveys and administrative databases to ensure greater coherence and accuracy in reporting.
ca.keyPoints:
• The NFHS-6 preliminary factsheets are designed as a concise snapshot, covering 101 major indicators of India's health and demographic trends.
• Indicators like sanitation and clean cooking fuel coverage are monitored via dedicated platforms such as Swachh Survekshan Grameen and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) surveys.
• Key demographic data, including mortality and birth registration, continue to be generated through the Sample Registration System (SRS), Civil Registration System (CRS), and the Census framework.
• Haemoglobin testing for anaemia was excluded from NFHS-6 due to methodological concerns regarding capillary blood sampling used in previous rounds.
• A comprehensive national report will be released subsequently, offering a broader analytical picture and detailed methodological documentation.
ca.whyInNews: The Union Health Ministry addressed media criticism regarding the 'missing' indicators in the NFHS-6 preliminary factsheets, clarifying the government's approach to data dissemination.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II (Governance/Health); Prelims: NFHS methodology, MoSPI, SRS, CRS, and Census; Mains: Data-driven policy making, challenges in health statistics, and inter-ministerial data coordination.

ca.title: India’s pension scheme lags in terms of coverage, contribution
ca.summary: The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) is facing a critical crisis due to the stagnation of the central government's contribution at ₹200 since 2007, which has been severely eroded by inflation. This inadequacy in financial assistance, coupled with a stagnant beneficiary base despite a rising elderly population, highlights a significant gap in India's social security framework.
ca.keyPoints:
• The central government's contribution to IGNOAPS remains fixed at ₹200 per month for the 60-plus age group, a figure unchanged since 2007.
• Inflation has eroded the real value of the ₹200 assistance to approximately ₹99 in current terms, necessitating an increase to at least ₹353 to restore original purchasing power.
• While the central contribution is stagnant, state governments have increasingly stepped in with top-up contributions, leading to significant regional disparities in pension amounts.
• Data reveals a widening gap between the number of actual beneficiaries (approx. 2.2 crore) and the projected elderly population, indicating a failure to expand coverage in line with demographic shifts.
• Surveys indicate that over 95% of beneficiaries cite rising costs of essential items as the primary reason for the inadequacy of the current pension amount.
ca.whyInNews: The issue has gained prominence following the 2025 Public Accounts Committee (PAC) report and an independent evaluation commissioned by the Ministry of Rural Development, both of which highlighted the urgent need for a revamp of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP).
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II: Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections of the population and issues relating to poverty and hunger. Prelims: National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), IGNOAPS eligibility criteria, and the role of the Ministry of Rural Development. Mains: Challenges in social security, fiscal federalism in welfare delivery, and the impact of inflation on social protection floors.

ca.title: ICMR
ca.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) is undergoing a strategic transformation to bridge the gap between biomedical research and grassroots healthcare delivery. By establishing a decentralized network of regional research institutes and launching the National Health Research Programme (NHRP), the ICMR aims to shift from project-based funding to solution-oriented public health outcomes.
ca.keyPoints:
• ICMR is repositioning itself as the apex body for biomedical research by integrating research outputs directly into state and district health systems.
• The establishment of a nationwide network of regional National Institutes of Health Research ensures localized operational research, spanning from Dibrugarh to Jodhpur.
• The National Health Research Programme (NHRP) identifies 13 critical priority areas, including antimicrobial resistance, tuberculosis, mental health, and nutrition.
• The initiative marks a paradigm shift from traditional project-based funding models to an integrated continuum focused on enabling actionable health solutions.
• Decentralization of research infrastructure aims to address regional health disparities and improve the efficacy of public health interventions on the ground.
ca.whyInNews: The ICMR is in the news for its structural reorganization and the launch of the National Health Research Programme, aimed at aligning biomedical research with India's evolving public health requirements.
ca.upscAngle: GS Paper II (Health, Governance, Statutory Bodies). Prelims: Role of ICMR, NHRP objectives. Mains: Strengthening public health infrastructure, evidence-based policy making, and decentralized governance in healthcare. Key terms: Biomedical Research, Operational Research, Public Health Continuum.

ca.title: From borderland to India's strategic resource frontier
ca.summary: The Government of India is reframing the Northeast from a sensitive, security-focused borderland into a "strategic resource frontier," driven by the need for critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, rare earth elements) essential for modern technologies and energy transitions.
ca.keyPoints:
Key Shift: Northeast states are increasingly identified as "quiet mineral frontiers" and "resource-rich frontiers."

Target Minerals: Lithium, cobalt, graphite, nickel, vanadium, chromium, and rare earth elements (REEs).

Applications: Critical for industrial competition, technological manufacturing, energy transitions, batteries, semiconductors, renewable technologies, and defense systems.

Current Status: India is heavily dependent on imports for these critical minerals.

Recent Exploration Push: * Agency: Geological Survey of India (GSI).

Scope: Undertook 43 critical mineral exploration projects across Northeastern states (covering the 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 field seasons).

States Involved: Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Assam, Nagaland, and Manipur.

Specific Project (Manipur): Recent initiation of exploration for nickel, cobalt, and chromium.
ca.upscAngle: GS 3 Environment

quiz.q: World Oceans Day, recently in the news, is observed annually on which date?
quiz.exp: World Oceans Day is observed on 8 June each year. The idea emerged at the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro and was officially recognized by the United Nations in 2008.

quiz.q: Which body of water separates Madagascar from the African mainland?
quiz.exp: The Mozambique Channel lies between Madagascar and Mozambique. It is the world's widest channel and an important route for currents, shipping and marine biodiversity in the western Indian Ocean.
